set.body:
Outcome: turn the strongest Volregger benchmark ideas into a reproducible, versioned court for reframe4s-motion without adding filesystem or external-tool dependencies to the published motion artifact.

Acceptance criteria:
AC-430-01: An unpublished benchmark project depends on reframe4s-motion and image4s-nifti; reframe4s-motion itself remains filesystem- and NIfTI-independent.
AC-430-02: AFNI 3dvolreg and FSL MCFLIRT are required 4D comparators. Pairwise FLIRT may be included in the pair-estimator court. RNiftyReg and nifreeze may be secondary comparators, with absence represented explicitly rather than silently skipped.
AC-430-03: Every required executable, container, dependency, dataset, and scenario is pinned by version or digest and recorded with a checksum and license or provenance note.
AC-430-04: Comparator transforms are recovered into one declared physical convention. Synthetic convention fixtures prove direction, handedness, center, world affine, and reference-frame conversion before accuracy scores are accepted.
AC-430-05: The court includes independent full-affine continuous phantoms, real-anatomy truth injection rendered independently of the candidate resampler, and native real runs. It covers null, low, moderate, hard, nuisance, capture-range, anisotropic, oblique, permuted, and reflected cases where supported.
AC-430-06: Registered claim metrics include exact relative-transform error, rotation angle, physical landmark displacement median and p95, framewise-displacement error, failure rate, corrected-image NRMSE and correlation, boundary error, temporal fidelity, edge preservation, and high-frequency residual or ringing. DVARS and tSNR remain diagnostic, not truth.
AC-430-07: Performance comparisons declare estimate, apply, and report stages; interpolation and resampling count; thread policy; warm-up; repetitions; median and p95 runtime; allocation where observable; peak RSS; temporary bytes; checksums; and visible failures.
AC-430-08: Metric directions, materiality tolerances, scenario weights, and the release pass rule are committed before candidate results are inspected. Changing them requires a new versioned protocol and receipt.
AC-430-09: Manual and scheduled automation fails when required comparators or datasets are missing, archives machine-readable raw and summary receipts, and produces a concise human audit with every material win, tie, loss, and unavailable optional result visible.
AC-430-10: mig-415 cannot authorize duplicate removal until the latest canonical revision has zero unwaived material losses in the predeclared high-value transform and image-fidelity families, satisfies absolute correctness gates, and has an explicit runtime and memory disposition.
set.title: EPIC: Establish the reproducible external motion evidence court
